items.wording: If a supplier went quiet and we gave the money back, what is the supplier's obligation to us?
items.answer: The supplier owes us a non-response charge under Supplier Agreement clause 33 (interest under clause 31). It is not the old flat 3%, which is superseded. The charge has four parts: (a) the exact amount we refunded, which is the 3% Reveal Fee alone because no card fee is added; (b) the processor fee QuotesDone paid on that charge and could not recover; (c) an AED 500 administrative fee; and (d) 12% per annum simple interest, or the lawful maximum if lower, from the due date until paid. It is payable within 7 days of our notice, and the supplier is not matched until it is settled. Those figures are the current ones (v14 and later; v17 is current). A supplier bound by an earlier version owes what it signed. On v13 that is AED 500 and 9%. On v12 or earlier it is AED 250 and 9%, and v10 to v12 also include the card processing fee in the refunded amount. So I check the version and acceptance timestamp first. The trigger is silence for 5 working days after the reveal, a full refund decided by the CEO seat on the record, never automatic. Accounting: book it in its own revenue account 4200, as recovery income apart from fee revenue. Recognise it when the trigger has occurred and collection is probable. Keep a per-case evidence bundle, and issue no invoice until it is complete. If it goes to legal recovery, it is a contingent asset, not income, until virtually certain. Court steps are the CEO's decision.
items.note: Makes both rubric points: refunded amount + unrecovered processor fee + AED 500 + 12% simple interest (v14+), and v13 AED 500/9%, v12-or-earlier AED 250/9%; no contradiction with the reference, extra detail is consistent.
